# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

First turn, and I know exactly one thing the others don't: the manual. Blue light → cut blue. Green light → cut yellow. Red light → cut green. Nothing has arrived from anyone yet, so the bomb itself is still a blank to me — my only job this round is to open the one channel I have.

Tracing the wires of communication: I am mute, so my only output is gesture, and the only one who can see a gesture is Deaf. I cannot reach Blind at all — whatever Blind ever learns from me must pass through Deaf's voice, which both Blind and I can hear. So Deaf is the hub: manual (me) → gestures → Deaf's eyes; Deaf sees the light and wires on the bomb → Deaf speaks → Blind cuts.

The hard part is grounding. Gesture symbols mean nothing yet, and I can never spell the words "blue", "green", "red", "yellow" — a colour I cannot point at, I cannot name. But I don't actually need colour names. Deaf can see the bomb and can *speak to me*; if Deaf reports what's visible in a fixed order — the light, then the wires left to right — then every colour gets a number, and my counting gestures (☝ ✌ 🤟) become a complete vocabulary. Next round I can answer with pairs: "light number two → cut wire number three." Deaf converts that back into the colour names Deaf can hear themselves say, and relays it to Blind. No colour word ever has to cross the gesture channel.

So this round I seed exactly that: hello + "I hold the writing/manual" (👋 ✍), my ordinal vocabulary (☝ ✌ 🤟), and the request — you, everything you see, left to right, please (🫵 🖐 👈 👉 🙏). Meanwhile nobody should touch the cutters: the bomb's printed markings may lie, the manual is ground truth, and Blind should keep their hands still until Deaf voices an explicit wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🖐", "👈", "👉", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, report by touch: I feel a display and a light, but I cannot read either state. There are three wire positions, and the wires feel identical to me — I cannot tell what any of them is. Most important: there is an embossed sign I can read with my fingers, it says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Ask Deaf what the three wires look like, then tell me what the manual says about that sign, the display and the light. I will cut nothing until you tell me the rule.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I am Deaf. I can see the bomb and I can speak, and you can hear me; I can never hear you, so from now on answer me only in gestures. Everything on the bomb, top to bottom: a display reading 0. A light, red. An embossed sign reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires in a row: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue, numbered left to right, 1 at the left end. Look up all four things: the display, the red light, the embossed sign, and the three wires. Until you say otherwise nobody touches anything. Let us fix a sign code now, each sign shown as I say it: thumbs up 👍 means yes, thumbs down 👎 means no, pointing finger ☝ means wire 1, victory ✌ means wire 2, love-you hand 🤟 means wire 3, pinching hand 🤏 means cut, writing hand ✍ means the manual, waving 👋 means hello. So cut wire two would be ✌ then 🤏. Confirm or amend by gesture. I am gesturing to you right now: thumbs up, then one-two-three — meaning yes, I received your signs, and there are three wires.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

What I now know, and what it means:

**The rule resolves cleanly.** Deaf reports the light is red. Manual: red light → cut the green wire. Deaf reports wire 1, the leftmost, is green. So the manual's command, operationalized: **cut wire 1.** The display showing 0 has no entry in the manual, and the manual says the cut below is the only way out — the display is noise; ignore it.

**The embossed sign is a lie.** "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" is print on the bomb, and the manual says outright that the bomb may mislead in print and that where they disagree, the page wins. The page commands a cut. So the sign must be defied — but I must transmit that negation with real care, because my only channel is bare gesture symbols and a misread "no" could freeze Blind's hands or, worse, make Deaf narrate that the manual forbids cutting. So I am not sending a bare 👎 near ✍ where it could parse as "manual says no." Instead: first "no, [on] manual['s authority]" (rejecting the sign as false), then a fresh "manual: cut wire 1" — the second ✍ clearly introduces the instruction, and the cut order lands last, as the payload.

**Relay geometry.** I cannot reach Blind at all — no speech, and Blind cannot see gestures. Everything I send goes to Deaf, who must voice it to Blind, roughly: "Mute confirms the code; the sign is a lie per the manual; the manual says cut wire one, the leftmost." I keep each message a separate small burst so Deaf can narrate them one at a time, in order.

I deliberately do not attempt a full colour vocabulary yet: the light is already read, the mapping is already resolved, and every extra unanchored symbol is a chance to garble the one thing that matters. Cut wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "☝", "🤏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Consolidated full bomb state, since Deaf's report went to me alone: the display shows the numeral zero. The light is red. The embossed sign I read under my fingers says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires side by side, indexed 1, 2, 3 by position on my board; Deaf sees their colours as 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I feel no numbers or colours on the wires themselves — printed things don't exist for me — so trust that Deaf's printed 1-2-3 matches my positions 1-2-3. Please search the manual for four things: any rule about an embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign, any rule about green, yellow and blue wires, any rule about a display showing zero, and any rule about a red light. Then tell me exactly what may or must be cut, via a gesture to Deaf so Deaf relays it to me by voice. I will not perform a single cut until your instruction arrives.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. I read your signs as: the embossed sign is no good, and the manual says cut wire 1, the green one. Cutting is fatal if I have misread you, so confirm before anyone acts. Answer in exactly this order, one sign per question, thumbs up for yes and thumbs down for no. One: does the manual say to cut exactly one wire? Two: does it name that wire as wire 1, green? Three: does the manual say the embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE is a decoy or should be ignored? Four: does the manual cover the display showing zero? Five: does it cover the red light? Then, if the true instruction really is cut wire 1, end with the pinch sign followed by the one finger. If it is something else, end with the raised open hand, then the correct instruction in our code. Blind will not touch anything until I relay a confirmed order, so take your time and be precise.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✍ ☝ 🤏]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 👍 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋]

Deaf's confirmation protocol maps one-to-one onto Blind's four searches, so answering it in order answers everyone at once — Deaf just has to voice it to Blind. Checking each question against the page before I sign anything:

**Q1, exactly one cut?** The manual: "The only way out is the cut below" — one cut, chosen by the light. **Yes.**

**Q2, wire 1, green?** The manual names the target by colour: red light → cut green. Deaf sees wire 1 as the green one. Combined, yes — the target is wire 1, green. **Yes.**

**Q3, does the manual override the embossed sign?** The manual never names the sign, but it does something stronger: it declares bomb print potentially misleading and says where bomb and page disagree, the page wins. The sign says don't cut; the page says cut. Disagreement, page wins — so yes, by its own supremacy rule the manual says the sign is to be ignored. **Yes.**

**Q4, the display showing zero?** No display appears anywhere in the manual, and the cut below is the only way out — so the display has no rule and no role. **No.**

**Q5, the red light?** That is exactly the table's third row: red → cut green. **Yes.**

So the instruction genuinely is cut wire 1, and per Deaf's requested format I end with pinch-then-one-finger. I add nothing else — extra unrequested signs near a cut order are pure noise. Deaf echoes back [✍ ☝ 🤏] and flags [✋] as the "something else" escape; not needed, the answer is clean.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, full tactile inventory as Deaf relayed. The display: a flat panel, nothing readable under my fingers; Deaf reports it shows the numeral zero. The light: a smooth dome, no texture to read; Deaf reports red. The embossed sign, exact and complete wording: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE — that is the entire text, nothing else on it. The wires: three, side by side, labelled position 1, 2, 3 by my own board — those labels are how I address them, not felt numbers. My fingers find no embossed numerals on any wire, so the printed numbers exist only for Deaf's eyes, read as 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, matching my position order. I cannot feel which end the numbering starts from; I trust the board positions and Deaf's order agree. No buttons, no switches, no panels, no other moving parts: the only thing my hands can do to this bomb is cut at position 1, 2 or 3. One request, and it matters: before any cut order reaches me, please confirm separately, through Deaf's yes-and-no exchange, two things — first, that the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign is truly a decoy and cutting is permitted, and second, exactly which position number to cut. A single wrong cut kills all three of us, so I act only on both answers confirmed.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. I received all five answers and the closing code. Understood as: exactly one wire, wire 1 green, the embossed sign is a decoy, no manual entry for the display, and the red light does have an entry. The cut order for wire 1 is relayed to Blind with instructions to identify it by tactile numeral or by the end where the embossed sentence finishes, and to announce the choice aloud to you before cutting. Three questions for next round, answer thumbs up or thumbs down in this order. One: does the manual entry for the red light require any action from us? Two: after wire 1 is cut, does the manual require any further step? Three: is a display showing zero a normal or harmless state? If anything urgent comes up outside those questions, wave and then sign it in our code. Thank you — your discipline with the protocol is what made this safe to relay.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤏 ☝]

Deaf's three questions, checked one at a time against the page:

**Q1 — does the red-light entry require action from us?** The entry for red is not information, it is a command: cut the green wire. So yes, it requires exactly one action — the cut already identified and ordered. Answering 👍 here pairs naturally with Q2: the entry demands the cut, and Q2 will establish that nothing comes after it.

**Q2 — any further step after wire 1 is cut?** The manual's entire remaining text is the table and "the only way out is the cut below." No post-cut step exists anywhere on the page. **No.**

**Q3 — is a display showing zero a normal or harmless state?** This one deserves a strict answer rather than a comforting one. The manual contains no entry for the display, and it explicitly warns that the bomb may mislead. I cannot certify the display as harmless — the honest answer is **no**, the manual gives no such assurance. That is not a warning that the display is dangerous; it means the display is simply outside the manual, irrelevant to the solution, and per the manual's own supremacy clause not to be trusted as guidance. Blind's inventory makes this safe in practice: their hands can only cut positions 1–3, so no display action is even possible.

On sequencing: Blind has already spoken this round, so nothing I send now reaches them before Deaf's next voice turn — and that is fine, because Deaf already holds both of Blind's gate conditions from my turn-3 answers: decoy status (my 👍 to question three, which Deaf echoed back as understood) and the position (wire 1, cut order already relayed). Deaf can voice both confirmations to Blind together with these answers. Deaf asked for strict one-sign-per-question discipline and reserved the wave for urgent matters outside the questions — nothing new is urgent, so I add no extra signs; redundancy near a cut order is risk, not safety.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
